selections.comment: Tony Carroll has an excellent strike rate at Brighton, and he sends two out for this contest, and it is POP DANCER who is seemingly his main hope in this. The 11-time winner has been in very good form this season and comes into this contest off the back of a win at Goodwood in May, before going on to come 2nd twice and 1st once at this venue, going from a mark of 59 to 65. He is in cracking form at present and showed last time when coming 2nd that there is more to come from him at this mark. Fancy Dancer is a lightly raced sort but has won twice already, winning off the mark of 53 at Wolverhampton in May; she also won at Bath in June. She can go well here off her highest career mark so far. Virtue Temperance has won once off the mark of 56 back in September; that was at this venue. Therefore, she can go well here and fill the places.

And Monks Mead has been floating around this mark for a few runs now; he can run well and fill the places here for a yard, doing well this season.

Too Much Trevor is yet to win in 21 career starts but has placed on multiple occasions, and if he can replicate the 2nd place effort from Chepstow last time, then he could land another place finish here. And Monks Mead has been floating around this mark for a few runs now; he can run well and fill the places here for a yard, doing well this season.

selections.comment: ENROLLED is a three-year-old in pretty good form at the moment; placing back in March on his first start of the season, he has since gone on to win at Salisbury last time out and has since gone up 3 lbs in the weights after that effort. That was his first career win, and given the manner that he kept on well in the closing furlong after a slow start, it would suggest there is more to come from the James Fanshawe horse. Coming into this after a short break, he can go well and land back-to-back wins for the very first time. Mafnood has been running well at present since changing yards; if he can back up the effort from last time, then he can land another place effort here in this. And Man Of La Mancha has been in decent form since being gelded; he can run well in this and fill the places for a yard in great form at the moment.

He did disappoint when only managing 2nd at Leicester last time when a short-priced favourite; he can bounce back to form here and make it two wins in just five career runs for his "new" yard. Parisian Phoenix is yet to win in her career; however, she has only had four career runs, but she can build on that handicap debut from last time and go a few places better here. And last year's winner of this race, Chourmo, can have a say in the finish and fill the places.

She would need everything to go perfect for her, but given how she is running at present, she can finally get her head in front for the first time in eight career runs. Voltaic has run plenty of times in his career and has the experience on quite a few of these, but he is not the force of old and might have to settle with coming 2nd here, which would actually be a very decent run for him. And Ideal Guest has been running well without winning lately; he can go well and fill the places here.

selections.comment: WARRNAMBOOL is certainly not the most reliable but his claims on pick of form are hard to ignore and Nick Littmoden's gelding is taken to land this. His latest effort can be excused as he raced in the centre away from the action and was eased once beaten. Before that he ran ran ok but got too far back at Newbury over a mile, but his first two runs this term were much more encouraging and both came over course and distance when 4th and 5th and not beaten far. It's notable his career debut was also over this CD when a promising third. It's worth chancing he can bounce back under these conditions and open his account. Token Gesture, a CD winner on final start last term on nursery handicap debut looks the main danger. He made an encouraging, if slightly below par, season debut last time here over an inadequate 6f. Off a pound lower mark and back over a more suitable trip he should go close. Top-weight Havana Halo, the mount of Oisin Murphy, is feared even if disappointing last time. Before that she built on a promising debut to be beaten less than two lengths in a fair novice. She could make the frame

selections.comment: A trappy affair with none of the field truly firing and all with questions to answer. The most solid option looks to be SOUTH SHORE ISLAND who is yet to replicate his 2024 form this year but showed signs of finding his level off a sliding mark last time over 7f. He flatteneed out late then but looked more comfortable than at 6f, over which he's been campaigned prior this term, and that was a better race than this. Off a further pound drop he can get his career back on track. Valsharah could be the main threat. Charlie Hills's gelding has looked tapped for toe over 6f his last three runs but was placed twice over 7f before those, including when third of nine over CD on season bow in March beaten less than two lengths off a four pound higher mark than today. He can bounce back to something like his best and go close. Silca Bay is dangerous but 7f appears to stretch his stamina so Mighty Ruler looks better placed to reach the frame having shown much more encouragement over CD on his  penultimate run and having been dropped a further 3lbs after a below par run last time at Sandown (about three lengths behind the selection). He can do better back over this CD

selections.comment: The progressive DUBLIN BAY is clear pick and has an excellent opportunity to land the hat-trick. Ollie Sangter's gelding took a step forward on nursery handicap bow to open his account on penultimate start and then improved markedly again when cruising to another win last time off a 7lb rise. A further 6lb here is unlikely to stop the juggernaut. Demetrius looks to have been given a workable opening mark by the assessor for his nursery debut and could chase the selection home. Madman and Highlighting have claims but Grand Echo looks next best having shown a lot more latest on his first time on Polytrack and over 6f and has decent each way claims

selections.comment: Some very interesting newcomers could complicate matters for RULER OF TIME but Charlie Appleby's colt should prove a tough nut to crack having posted a hugely encouraging second on debut despite being pretty green. He should be able to build considerably on that and is clear pick given William Buick chooses him above stablemate National History making his debut. Charlie Appleby's second string was an expensive purhcase at the breeze-up sales and looks likely to have a bright future. He could give his stablemate most to do. Blue Aria and Lord D'Or are others making their debut that catch the eye and could figure but those looking for each way value should consider Looka who had a bit of a nightmare on debut after a slow start and then being denied a run for a while over 3f out before staying on well once in the clear. A much improved effort is on the cards and he could well reach the frame this time

selections.comment: Jewelry, returning from a lengthy absence to make her season debut, sets the standard of those with experience having won in style on debut last August. She disappointed when raised to Group company on second start when last seen trailing in last despite going off favourite. That was a backward step but she still showed enough then to have something in hand of those with experience here and a much improved effort looks likely now eased in class. However, she may be vulnerable to at least one of the eye-catching newcomers, with SHINARA, an expensive purchase as a yearling, demanding plenty of respect. She's a full sister to classy Charyn and her dam was a winner on the AW. Cotiere, another debutant to make plenty of appeal on paper, could also go close on debut given a hefty-price tag when purchased in the breeze-up sales and from a yard going great guns

selections.comment: The experienced Port Road has been going well in handicap company this term, mostly getting pretty competitive and rarely beaten far, and could find this company a bit easier. It would be no surprise to see Simon Dow's gelding get his head in front at long last (13 race maiden), however he could be vulnerable to one or two of the newcomers, namely Canopus (second choice) and Raammee and even more so the twice-raced VRONTI, who improved markedly on debut to go very close last time at Haydock. There should be a fair bit more to come from Richard Hannon's filly and if taking to this surface she has a good opportunity to open her account on third start

He stands out on an excellent second on debut at Southwell despite a slow start and havng to come from the rear to challenge a bit too late. If building on that he'll be tough to master. Earl Of Rochester looks the most likely to upset the selection having shown a similar standard on debut when a close-up third at Newmarket last year. His return run, when last seen in March, was disappointing, being turned over at odds-on. However, he's worth another chance to confirm his debut promise and could go close. Tardaff is interesting back up to a mile which based on his latest two efforts over 7f should help, even if she ran poorly over it on debut, but Alcarath, an expensive purchase, could pose a bigger threat on debut

Earl Of Rochester looks the most likely to upset the selection having shown a similar standard on debut when a close-up third at Newmarket last year. His return run, when last seen in March, was disappointing, being turned over at odds-on. However, he's worth another chance to confirm his debut promise and could go close. Tardaff is interesting back up to a mile which based on his latest two efforts over 7f should help, even if she ran poorly over it on debut, but Alcarath, an expensive purchase, could pose a bigger threat on debut

selections.comment: With all the field with something to prove, to a lesser or greater extent, a chance is taken on the admittedly risky CAPONE. Dominic Ffrench Davis's gelding is hugely frustrating and has not managed to post two solid efforts on the trot for two seasons now. However, when hitting form he's been very competitive, notably when a fine second over CD in mid-May off the same mark as today. That was his season opener and although pulled up next time, when something was obviously amiss, and then well beaten last time, he's sprung back to top form after a blip or two on plenty of occassions. If able to be in the vanguard early he could spring another shock eased back to this level. Synergism, at the top of his game, and Simiyann, not quite firing but capable off this kind of mark, are less risky options and both have fair claims. Synergism is preferred ahead of Simiyann. Letmebetheboss is likely to be on the premises and is another to consider
